Dispatched by the factory from `dev.task` [`22fffb20-bde4-4343-8ed5-c5931561c64d`](22fffb20-bde4-4343-8ed5-c5931561c64d).

**This PR was written by an agent and checked by the dispatcher.** The dispatcher
runs declared verification in the isolated clone before opening a PR. It
bootstraps a clone-local `venv/` from the repo's Python dependency declarations
and adds `PyYAML` because the committed EA/checker scripts import `yaml` without
owning that dependency in a requirements file. That path is slower than relying
on the host interpreter, but it keeps task specs faithful and makes
`venv/bin/python ...`, `python ...`, and `python3 ...` declarations resolve
inside the clone.

Change kind: behavioral

## Requirement refs

- PC-EXE-005/AC-9
- PC-EXE-005/AC-12

## Verification checkout

Declared verification below ran against `f9d8a8f42a46e873f8a0128bb810bc6c5137b6a9` of `main`. The dispatcher refuses to clone (so this PR would not exist) unless both hold at dispatch time: the worker checkout's own revision is a confirmed, current ancestor of local `main` (`worker_revision.ensure_checkout_is_current_with_main`), and `main` itself is a confirmed ancestor-or-equal of its own tracking upstream -- carries no commit absent from it (`dispatch.ensure_base_ref_current`; `BaseRefStatus.wrong`). Date this evidence against that commit, not against when the PR was opened.

This attempt resumed from preserved work: the latest of https://github.com/grantbest/homelabv2/pull/1181 was applied as the clone's starting point before the worker's first action (OPS-106). The revision above is the base the baseline was applied onto, not the tree verification ran against -- that tree is base + baseline + this attempt's work.

## Intent

R26.12 (docs/releases/R26.12.json, opens 2026-10-06; design docs/plans/2026-09-23-design-r2612-steerable-and-legible.md, DECIDED by the Operator 2026-09-24; sprint plan docs/plans/2026-09-25-sprints-55-57-the-queue-has-an-order-and-work-in-it.md with P1-P4 decided 2026-09-25). Common rules: dispatch.py and guards.py together are 8,530 lines at main 447d6174 and every merge must stay strictly below 8,556 (the arc budget), net negative at close [RE-BASELINED 2026-10-02 by the outer loop: the pair stood at 8,612 (7,229 + 1,383) at main 856071fe, so the absolute 8,556 no longer binds; the binding size rule is each bead's own net-growth bound in its ACs, measured against its own merge-base, and the arc closes at or below 8,612]; B2 (bead 7f41c574, spec S55-B2) creates apps/factory-dispatcher/queue_order.py and B7 (bead 75b459ca, spec S55-B7) adds rank_pending, RankPolicy, QueuePosition and QueueOrder to it, both PENDING and not merged at this drafting -- if queue_order.py or the names this spec builds on do not exist at your base, the predecessor has not merged: STOP and report unverified, do not re-implement them. Tests use the committed fixtures (tests/fixtures/queue-synthetic-2026-09-23.json, queue-2026-09-23-latched.json, release-inputs-2026-09-23.json, on main since #1026) and doubles only; never a store, a cluster or the live queue (decision record 2026-09-13 D7). The store-double ceiling tests/test_store_double_call_surface.py MAX_HAND_ROLLED_DOUBLES is 35 with zero headroom and counts cross-file subclasses and apps/mcp-hub/tests: extend an existing fake in place, add no new class carrying two or more store-protocol method names. Every spawn passes env= and every new spawn-bearing function gets a CASES entry in tests/test_spawn_env_fixture.py. Stage new files with git add before the final verification run. Build item B16 (design :146; pred B15, bead id set at filing). Two fences, both required before B8 makes the charters and the policy into ordering inputs (sprint plan release order step 3): nothing the factory writes may set its own class of service, and no lane may edit docs/releases/** (the charters, and from B0b docs/releases/policy/health-policy.json). At main 447d6174: apps/factory-dispatcher/contracts/task-intake-contract.json has keys required, forbidden_always and lanes, with forbidden_always the STRING '.github/workflows/**'; file_task.build_content appends it to every spec's forbidden_paths; apps/lifeops-console/src/lib/task-intake-contract.json is the console's copy, pinned byte-equal by tests/test_task_intake_contract_copy_parity.py; tests/test_dev_lanes_match_intake_contract.py also reads the contract; scanner.py SCANNER_FORBIDDEN_PATHS (:86) is a tuple beginning '.github/**', 'infrastructure/**', 'docs/requirements/**', 'ARCHITECTURE.md'; the hub's POST /api/v1/factory/tasks files through file_task.file_spec, so a refusal here is the same refusal over HTTP with no hub change (PC-FAC-001/AC-5). The store's DevTaskContent schema requires the literal '.github/workflows/**' in scope.forbidden_paths (the hand-filing memory of 2026-09-23), so the list form must still carry it first.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: THE MARKER FIELDS ARE REFUSED AT INTAKE. file_task.build_content (or the preflight that runs before it; one place, named in the PR body) refuses a spec whose top-level keys or whose content would carry class_of_service, expedite_reason or expedite_until, with SystemExit naming the field and saying the marker is set only by the operator verb (B17). tests/test_file_task.py::test_intake_refuses_class_of_service covers each of the three fields and a spec carrying none (accepted). The refusal reaches the hub route unchanged through file_spec (an existing hub access test is not modified; the PR body states that the route calls file_spec).
- AC-2: FORBIDDEN_ALWAYS IS A LIST, AND IT FENCES THE CHARTERS. task-intake-contract.json's forbidden_always becomes ['.github/workflows/**', 'docs/releases/**'] in the dispatcher's copy and, byte-identically, in the console's copy; build_content appends every entry to forbidden_paths (de-duplicated, '.github/workflows/**' still present so the store's schema is satisfied); every reader of the contract accepts the list form -- in Python tests/test_dev_lanes_match_intake_contract.py and any other found by grep for 'forbidden_always', and in TypeScript apps/lifeops-console/src/lib/dev-board.ts, whose TASK_FORBIDDEN_ALWAYS (:26 at 447d6174) and its uses (:127, :132) read the value as one string and would push an array into forbidden_paths (a store 422) and fail the console typecheck; dev-board.ts and dev-board.test.ts are updated so the console appends every entry -- and a string form is refused by one Python test so the shape cannot silently regress. file_task gains a refusal, which does not exist today, for a spec whose scope.paths intersects forbidden_paths (the same matcher guards.check_scope uses, so the refusal and the guard agree); tests/test_file_task.py::test_intake_refuses_docs_releases files a spec whose scope.paths names docs/releases/policy/health-policy.json and asserts the refusal cites forbidden_always; tests/test_task_intake_contract_copy_parity.py passes.
- AC-3: THE SCANNER. scanner.SCANNER_FORBIDDEN_PATHS gains 'docs/releases/**'; tests/test_scanner.py::test_scanner_forbids_docs_releases asserts a proposal touching docs/releases/ is refused; tests/test_scanner.py::test_scanner_content_has_no_class_of_service asserts the scanner's content builder emits none of the three marker keys.
- AC-4: EVERY EXISTING SPEC STILL BUILDS. The corpus test (tests/test_file_task.py, the `corpus` cases) passes: every committed spec under tasks/ still builds with the new forbidden_always, and the known-exceptions list is unchanged.
- AC-5: WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE. dispatch.py and guards.py are untouched (the PR body quotes `wc -l` of both at the base's values); nothing under apps/mcp-hub or apps/substrate changes; the console copy changes only to mirror the contract.
- AC-6: MUTATION. Each turns a test red: accepting expedite_reason alone; dropping '.github/workflows/**' from the list; the console copy left behind; a scanner proposal under docs/releases/ accepted; a reader that only accepts the string form.
- AC-7: REPORT. The PR body states the collected-test count before and after, the place the marker refusal lives, and the corpus count.

## Environment parity with CI

- **Neutralized:** ambient git config. Declared verification runs with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` pointed at `/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` set, so `init.defaultBranch` and any committer identity from the operator's `~/.gitconfig`, a conventional `/etc/gitconfig`, *or* a vendor-baked installation-scope config (Apple's git ships one CI has no equivalent of -- PR #792's gate caught that `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` alone doesn't hide it) are invisible to it, matching a CI runner that has none of the three (#765's `create_repo_with_tracking_main` specimen).
- **Reported, not neutralized:** this clone carries a local `main` branch tracking `origin/main`, because the dispatcher's own later git operations in this same clone need one. CI's `actions/checkout` on a PR instead leaves a detached HEAD with no local `main`. A declared command that depends on `main` being a resolvable ref -- not merely on config -- can still pass here and fail in CI (#759).
- **Undetectable by this pre-check:** anything not git-configuration or dependency-presence shaped -- network reachability, OS/platform differences, resource limits, and any ambient environment variable outside `VERIFICATION_ENV_ALLOWLIST` that CI also lacks. A green pre-check establishes parity only for the two points above, not general CI-equivalence.

[Corrected by the outer loop from the PR 1184 release gate's recount; the worker's report measured from the preserved baseline 910f6977.] Full suite: 2899 passed, 24 skipped. The marker-field refusal lives in `file_task._check_no_marker_fields`, called from `build_content` (file_task.py:1441-1471), which every intake path (CLI, hub route via `file_spec`, scanner's `content_for_filing`, console via the hub) runs through unchanged.
